Left out: Creative Bloq's Citroen 2CV opinion, Sour Patch Kids' billboard, Mother Design's talk page (no readable text), the member-only UX Collective essays on taste and the design hourglass, State of Brand on AI citations, Microsoft comms and LinkedIn copy-paste stories, illustrator and artist portraits, Creative Bloq deals and game reviews, and the TechCrunch, Ars Technica and MIT Technology Review general tech run (Character.AI's bankruptcy, Facebook's feed controls, robots, space). stories.title: Studiogusto turns Michelangelo's hand into a working script for St. Peter's
stories.blurb: The brief was not a replica but a functional script for signage inside the basilica, built from the Vatican's manuscripts. Where the archive had no modern numerals, the team derived them from letters, the 1 from the I, across more than 500 characters in four styles. The font now ships in Microsoft 365.

sources.name: Creative Bloq
sources.headline: How Michelangelo’s handwriting became a Microsoft font

stories.title: Pentagram's Design Doha identity gives Arabic and English equal weight
stories.blurb: There is no static logo: both scripts sit inside the same typographic compositions, and stretched strokes run across layouts like map lines. A travertine beige and maroon ground the palette, the inaugural edition's blue carries over. The headline exhibition gets a heavier variant of the same logic.

sources.name: Design Week
sources.headline: Pentagram creates dynamic bilingual identity for Design Doha Biennial 2026

stories.title: Barkas moves Kuda out of the challenger-bank look
stories.blurb: The brief was to take the Nigerian bank from challenger to established, and the answer drops gradients and smiling flat characters entirely. A stacked KU/DA mark drawn from Nigerian art and architecture, a custom Naira sign made with local partners, and documentary photography by Nigerian photographers carry the 'More Life' line.

sources.name: It's Nice That
sources.headline: “Less bank, more life”: Barkas gives Nigerian digital bank Kuda an identity with the pace of Lagos

stories.title: Studio Herrström builds Milkshake's identity from car rides and carton labels
stories.blurb: The Sony Music label previewed its demos in cars, so the studio took cues from roadside settings and vehicle detail. Information lockups copy car window permits and milk carton nutrition tables to hold track titles, dates and copyright lines.

sources.name: Design Week
sources.headline: STUDIO HERRSTR M draws on car culture and carton typography for Milkshake rebrand

stories.title: Altra answers a quitting statistic with four runners aged 75 to 85
stories.blurb: Commissioned research says British runners stop at 39 on average, mostly through injury, which is bad news for a brand built on running for life. Brandnation found the cast through desk research in club news, race results and local press, and Rankin shot them.

sources.name: Creative Boom
sources.headline: Britain s oldest running team has a combined age of 321, and Rankin shot their portraits

stories.title: Brands now have to be chosen twice, first by the customer's AI
stories.blurb: An Australian Centre for AI in Marketing report, backed by Adobe, argues the first selection now happens out of marketers' sight. In the cited survey of 1,736 Australians, 39 percent had used generative AI to pick a brand, but only 11 percent would let it make a purchase. A press release, so the numbers are the report's own.

sources.name: Roastbrief
sources.headline: The customer journey no longer starts with the customer ACAM report warns

stories.title: A free AI-coded Creative Cloud clone, tested
stories.blurb: Brandon Thomas vibe-coded seven Adobe look-alikes in Rust with Claude Opus 5.5, each around 50MB. Creative Bloq's test finds the controls where you expect them but harsh sharpening, imprecise masking and no camera profiles: just usable, not a replacement. Creative Boom asks whether this is design software's Napster moment.

sources.name: Creative Bloq
sources.headline: I tried those free AI-coded Adobe Creative Cloud clones, and they have some big problems

sources.name: Creative Boom
sources.headline: AI just cloned Adobe s apps for free. Is this design software s Napster moment?

stories.title: Google ships Gemini 4 Argon at a fifth of rival prices
stories.blurb: Google claims Argon beats GPT-6 Astra and Claude's top models on several benchmarks and cuts down on hedging and stock phrases. The introductory price is $2 per million input and $10 per million output tokens, doubling at the end of November. In the Gemini app it is for paying users only.

stories.title: Google Play now runs vibe-coded apps privately on your own phone
stories.blurb: Apps built with AI can now be installed on your Android device through your Google account without being published to the store. Sharing with others is announced for the coming months. Until now, running one natively meant publishing it to all Play users, which kept many people on web apps.
